rationale: No suitable optimization is supported for this workflow. The workflow already implements dependency caching via Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 in three jobs and apt package caching via cache-apt-pkgs-action in the fmt-crank-check job, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is contraindicated (an equivalent cache already exists). The tests job already carries an explicit timeout-minutes: 60. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT could add timeouts to the three jobs lacking them, but the CI history shows high run-to-run variability (8-34 minutes total) without per-job duration data, so setting safe timeout budgets risks cutting off valid slow runs, which matches the pattern contraindication that valid slow runs may exceed the proposed limit. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply because no job uses a matrix strategy. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE would require a new action and workflow permissions to call the GitHub API, conflicting with the constraint against adding privileged actions or new network access. Remaining patterns (scheduled workflow suppression, Bazel builds, test selection/prioritization, environment reuse) do not apply to this pull-request/push Rust workflow.
